visuals.heading: 5 Research Lanes for Humanities Graduates

items.text: Here is the full picture before the detail.
All five of those are real, current jobs in India today.

blocks.heading: Underneath the Five Very Different Job Titles

items.text: Turning a messy pile of interviews, documents, or data into one clear, defensible finding
Every one of these five lanes pays for the same underlying move: synthesis.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The one skill that decides your pay in every lane

blocks.heading: Not Have to Pick

items.text: You do not have to pick a research lane by guessing which one sounds most impressive at a family gathering.
For academic research, write one short literature review.
A 20-minute honest conversation with a working policy analyst, market researcher, UX researcher, or M&E coordinator tells you more about the daily reality than a semester of reading about the field.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Test a lane before you commit years to it

items.text: An academic historian, a policy analyst, a UX researcher, and an NGO M&E officer do genuinely different daily work, for different pay, on different timelines.
A PhD is the longest, lowest-paying, and highest-commitment lane on this list.

visuals.title: 5 Research Lanes for Humanities Graduates

visuals.alt: A comparison table for Compare the Practical Paths.
visuals.caption: Compare the listed options.
visuals.heading: Compare the Practical Paths

rows: UX research
People who like one-on-one interviews, usability testing, and translating human behaviour into product decisions.
Entry-level UX researchers with under a year of experience earn roughly Rs 5.4 lakh a year on average; this climbs toward Rs 9.5 lakh by 1-4 years with a portfolio.
Market and consumer research
People who want faster corporate entry and are comfortable mixing surveys, interviews, and basic data reading.
Entry-level market research analyst pay in India runs roughly Rs 5-8 LPA, rising to Rs 10-18 LPA by 3-6 years with quantitative skills like SQL.
Policy and think tank research
People who liked analysis, current affairs, and writing structured notes more than a narrow academic thesis.
Entry-level policy analyst pay commonly runs Rs 5-9 LPA, but research-associate-level roles at smaller think tanks can start closer to Rs 2.5-4 LPA.
Social-sector and NGO research (M&E)
People who want research work with a visible social outcome, and can tolerate lower starting pay for mission-driven work.
Entry-level roles often start around Rs 20,000-50,000 a month; monitoring-and-evaluation managers at larger NGOs later reach Rs 12-22 LPA.
Academic research (NET-JRF, PhD, assistant professor)
People who want deep subject mastery and are genuinely willing to spend 5-8+ years before stable income.
JRF stipend is Rs 37,000/month for the first two years. Only the top 6% of NET-qualified candidates get a JRF slot at all. Assistant professor posts are scarce relative to PhD output.

figures.source: Government college assistant professor basic pay starts near Rs 57,700 (Level 10), roughly Rs 90,000-1.1 lakh gross with allowances once you get a post.
